dialog.body: Utilities Division, this is Priya. How can I help you?
Hi, yes, good morning. Um, my name is Anh Nguyen. I think I'm calling about my water bill, maybe the sewer part too. It sort of looks wrong to me.
Okay, Ms. Nguyen. Can you give me the service address so I can pull up the account?
Yeah, it's 200 Bacheller Street. I think it's in the Fifth Ward, if that matters. I'm renting, but the bill comes to me, I'm pretty sure.
Got it, one moment. I have the account here for 200 Bacheller. What looks off about the bill?

So, a new meter was put in last month, I think it was early December, maybe the first week. And this bill is, I mean, it's sort of double what I usually pay. Nothing changed in the house. Same people, same everything.
I see the meter exchange on the account. The first bill after a new meter can reflect a different reading method. Let me look at the actual reads. Do you have the bill in front of you?
Yeah, I have it. It says, I think, the current reading is something like 4,812 and the previous one is, um, maybe 4,790? That doesn't seem like double. But the amount is high.
Hold on. Those numbers are close together, which would be a small usage. Let me check whether the old meter's final read was entered correctly. Can you stay on for a minute?
Sure, I'm not going anywhere. [pause] Sorry, I have the game on in the other room, it's, uh, football, the college one. It's loud.
No problem. I'll be right back.
Okay. [pause] Oh, nice, yes! Good catch. Sorry. Quietly. Okay.

Thanks for holding. So the old meter's final reading was recorded, and the new one starts from a fresh number. It looks like the system may have billed the gap between the two incorrectly. I'm seeing a usage figure that is much higher than your history.
See, that's what I thought. I think it's wrong. I'm not paying for something I sort of didn't use.
Understood. One other thing I'd ask: has there been any leak or plumbing work at the house recently? Sometimes a repair changes usage, and it's good to rule it out.
Yeah, actually, we had a plumber out maybe two weeks ago for a kitchen faucet. I kept the receipt. I think it was just the faucet, nothing running or leaking after.

Good, hang on to that receipt. It helps show the usage wasn't from a leak. I'm going to flag the account for a meter read verification and a billing review. Someone from the meter team will confirm the reading.
Okay. So, do I have to pay this bill now? Like it's due, I think, the end of the month, maybe?
I'll put a note on the account that the bill is under review. Until it's corrected, I'd hold off on paying the disputed amount, and a corrected bill will be issued if the reading is wrong.
Alright. And, um, in general, if I need to pay a bill later, is there a way to pay by phone after 4:30? I work, so I usually can't get there before you close.

Yes. You can pay online through the city's website at any hour. There's also a drop box at City Hall for checks that's available after hours. And the automated payment line takes payments by phone when the office is closed.
Oh, okay, the automated line, that's good. I think I have the account number on the bill. Is it the long one at the top?
The account number is on the upper right of the statement. It should be labeled. If you have trouble, call back and we can read it with you.
Okay, I'll look. Um, and you said somebody will come check the meter? Do I have to be home? I sort of work days.

If the meter is outside or in the basement that's accessible, they may not need you. I'll note that you're a renter and that the reader may need access. Can I confirm a callback number in case they need to reach you?
Yeah, it's 401-555-0155. That's my cell. I think it's okay to leave a message.
401-555-0155, got it. I'll add a note to leave a voicemail if there's no answer. And can you hold onto the plumber receipt, in case the billing team asks for a copy?
Yeah, I have it in the kitchen drawer. I can take a picture if somebody wants it.
That works. They'll tell you how to send it. You should hear back within a few business days, maybe sooner with the storm coming, so give it a little extra time.
Right, the storm. I think it's supposed to start this afternoon. Anyway. It's just, I don't know, a hassle. But okay. Thank you.
I understand. Thanks for calling, Ms. Nguyen, and stay safe in the weather today.
You too. Bye.
